chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Mansur al-Siqall, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

There is no objection to a man enjoying [temporary marriage] with two sisters; this does not contradict the report because the apparent meaning of the report does not specify whether he enjoys them simultaneously or separately. And since that is not explicit in its apparent meaning, we interpret it as permitting enjoyment with one after the other, rather than simultaneous enjoyment of both.

key_terms.يَتَمَتَّعُ: enjoys (referring to temporary marriage or Mut'ah)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to be in a temporary marriage with two sisters at the same time?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq to clarify the scope of the prohibition on marrying two sisters simultaneously in temporary marriage (Mut'ah). The Imam employs the principle of *takhsis* (specification) or *haml* (interpretation), arguing that since the general text does not explicitly forbid simultaneous union, the default assumption is that the prohibition applies only to simultaneous marriage, thereby permitting sequential marriage with each sister individually.
